clue.text: Rob's chucking snowballs at head — duck!

indicators.note: chucking means throwing away, so a letter is dropped from the word for rob

parts.note: Rob's reads as 'rob is'; to rob is to steal

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the leading letter of snowballs is used

explanation.surface: A warning shout as Rob hurls snowballs at someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck!' looks like a cry to dodge, but it is the bird. 'chucking' removes S, the first letter of snowballs ('at head'), from STEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater species of dabbling duck.

clue.text: Finally in town at foot of mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue, being at the foot of something means coming after it below

parts.note: the Atlas Mountains run across north-west Africa
T is a standard abbreviation for town, as on maps

explanation.surface: Arriving at last in a town nestled beneath the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue T (town) is placed under ATLAS, so 'at foot of' says it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mark something happening in the end, after a long wait.

clue.text: Applauded the end of Trump in relief

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of Trump is taken

parts.note: carving in relief stands out from its background, that is, it is raised

explanation.surface: People cheered with relief when Trump's time was over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in relief' looks like a feeling of ease; here it is the sculptural sense, raised from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to commend them, as applause does.

clue.text: Weight having hit maturity

parts.note: to pound is to hit repeatedly
coming of age is reaching maturity

explanation.surface: Someone putting on weight just as they reach middle age.
explanation.definitionFit: Poundage is a weight expressed in pounds, as for a bow's draw or a person's bulk.

clue.text: Sack agent nearly filled delivering notices

indicators.note: to sack a city is to wreck and plunder it, so these letters are thrown into disorder
nearly means not quite all of the word filled, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An employer firing a postal agent who had nearly finished distributing notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissal but signals an anagram of AGENT plus FILLE ('filled' less its last letter, 'nearly').
explanation.definitionFit: Handing out printed flyers door to door or in the street is the activity named by the answer.

clue.text: Target men? I don't agree

parts.note: a target is an object, the thing aimed at
OR, other ranks, is military shorthand for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether to aim at the soldiers refuses outright.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the person it describes: one who says 'I don't agree'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter, voicing protest, is someone who raises objections.

clue.text: Citizen of Belgium sounded strange

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

indicators.note: sounded means the word for strange is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: rummy is an old British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A Belgian national whose accent struck listeners as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is a native of Birmingham, England's second city; 'Citizen' stands for one with the B supplied by Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brummie is a resident of Birmingham, so a citizen of that city.

clue.text: Affected collie's eyes

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of collie are reworked

parts.note: the word collie, with the 's read as 'has'

explanation.surface: A sheepdog's eyes have been affected by some ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelli are simple eyes, as found in insects and other invertebrates.

clue.text: Italian soldier under him at Crécy

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the soldier below the French pronoun

parts.note: Crécy is in France, where him is lui
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An Italian soldier serving beneath a commander at the battle of Crécy.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi is a common Italian forename, so an Italian man.

clue.text: (Starting here) clue to Nina maybe suggests a scientific process

indicators.note: maybe says these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A solver is told that a hidden message in the grid begins here and hints at science.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nina is a hidden message in a grid; the clue says this entry is where one starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nucleation is the first step in forming crystals or bubbles, a process studied in physics and chemistry.

clue.text: French busy making short film

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a flick is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: A Parisian policeman is shooting a short film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flic is French slang for a policeman, matching the slang 'busy'.

clue.text: Let me go out, grab club and prepare for fight

indicators.note: grab means the scrambled letters close round another piece
go out suggests the letters wander off and come back in a new order

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: Someone eager to brawl demands release and seizes a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' shuffles LET ME into EMTLE, and 'grab' puts BAT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle troops is to draw them up in battle array, readying them for combat.

clue.text: Spent the summer in east with Dave — it bombed

indicators.note: bombed suggests something blown apart, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A summer holiday out east with Dave went badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Aestivation is dormancy through hot dry months, the summer counterpart of hibernation.

clue.text: Expert help over lethargy

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A skilled helper can cure listlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Acedia is spiritual sloth or apathy, a torpor of the soul.

clue.text: 'Drinks on me!' (First of several errors)

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the drinks follow the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first of several is its opening letter

parts.note: sups are sips or drinks

explanation.surface: Someone buying a round, then making the first of many mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Botches and blunders are things done badly, the same as mistakes.

clue.text: Trendy pair are opening up to musician

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read from bottom to top
pair means the word for trendy appears twice

parts.note: in means fashionable
an are is a metric unit of area, 100 square metres, abbreviated A
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A fashionable couple become fans of a famous violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ININ + A + GAP backwards, reading upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated Italian violin virtuoso and composer.

clue.text: English tart reclining in lead vehicle for hire

indicators.note: in places the English and reversed tart letters inside the lead symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: reclining means lying back, so the word for tart is reversed

parts.note: tart means sour, or acid

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman lounging in the front cab of a hired vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a woman but means sour; 'reclining' turns that word round to give DICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered rickshaw that carries paying passengers.

clue.text: A shot on table, drunkard finally gathered

parts.note: a masse is a billiards shot struck with a near-vertical cue

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of drunkard

explanation.surface: A billiards shot made by a drinker, at the end of a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, so gathered.

clue.text: Engine drivers, after crash, stop in seconds

indicators.note: after a crash things lie wrecked and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Train drivers bring things to a halt within seconds after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engine drivers' suggests train crews, but means engine parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistons move in cylinders and drive an engine's crankshaft.

clue.text: Rowing over an item of jewellery

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
an is the indefinite article, a
a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: A quarrel about a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing' looks like quarrelling but is pulling oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Propelling a boat with oars is rowing.

clue.text: National craze rightfully adopted

indicators.note: adopted means taken in, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A country adopts a fashion, and quite properly so.
explanation.definitionFit: An Azeri is a person from Azerbaijan, a national of that state.

clue.text: Big-time writer releasing book — comeback essential

indicators.note: comeback means everything is read backwards

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a nib is a pen point, the part that writes

explanation.surface: A famous author drops a book and stages a vital comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' takes B from NIB, leaving NI; 'comeback' reverses LARGE + T + NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral is fundamental, a necessary part of the whole.

clue.text: Authoritarian type regularly stays talking crosswords

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of stays

parts.note: read as talking cross words, angry speech, which is ranting

explanation.surface: A strict person who keeps going on about crossword puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosswords' splits into cross words; the setter, Tyrus, may be teasing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot or oppressive ruler is the classic authoritarian figure.

clue.text: Divine female getting hard time

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A lovely woman going through a tough spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine female' sounds like a compliment but means goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the queen of the Greek gods, a goddess.

clue.text: A bit of trouble fitting in — Lauren is struggling to adapt to new surroundings

indicators.note: fitting in means the letter is placed inside the scrambled letters
struggling suggests flailing about, so these letters are rearranged
a bit of the word trouble here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Lauren has some trouble settling into a new place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges LAUREN IS; A plus T, the first letter of trouble, goes inside ('fitting in').
explanation.definitionFit: Naturalising means acclimatising a person, plant or animal so it thrives in a new place.

clue.text: Go into dock after robbing President's place in France

indicators.note: after robbing means once a letter has been stolen from the phrase

parts.note: a ship that goes into dock to be laid up is said to lie up
P is the abbreviation for president

explanation.surface: A ship sails into dock after a raid on a president's property.
explanation.walkthrough: LIE UP loses P, the president, to leave the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu is the French noun for a location or spot.

clue.text: Woman the writer's inclined to pick up

indicators.note: to pick up means to catch the sound of the words

parts.note: the writer is I, the setter; inclined is lean, giving I lean

explanation.surface: A writer admits a tendency to seduce women.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a woman's first name.

clue.text: No plan to stop big player in games

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the word for plan goes inside no

parts.note: to plan something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A major sports figure is barred from playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big player in games' suggests a star athlete, but means a video-games company.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo is a giant of the video-game industry.
